question: What gas is commonly used to inflate the abdomen during laparoscopy?
explanation: Carbon dioxide is readily absorbed by body tissues and safely eliminated through the respiratory system during laparoscopy. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why is laparoscopy often preferred over traditional open surgery?

options.A: It eliminates the need for general anesthesia completely
options.B: It entirely prevents the occurrence of internal bleeding
options.C: It allows surgeons to perform procedures without any incisions
options.D: It results in smaller scars and quicker recovery times

explanation: Smaller cuts cause less body stress, less pain, and let patients get back on their feet much faster. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is one of the main reasons a doctor would order a laparoscopy?
explanation: Looking directly inside helps doctors find issues like endometriosis or scar tissue that regular scans might miss. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h2)

question: A patient scheduled for laparoscopic staging is most likely being evaluated for what condition?
explanation: Staging allows the surgical team to look directly at how far cancer has spread inside the belly. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which condition makes laparoscopic surgery unsafe to perform?

options.D: A body mass index over thirty

explanation: Blood clotting problems put the patient at high risk of heavy, uncontrollable bleeding when instruments are put in. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why do previous belly surgeries make laparoscopy more challenging?

options.A: They make carbon dioxide insufflation completely impossible
options.B: They increase the risk of accidental bowel injury from adhesions
options.C: They prevent the administration of general anesthesia safely
options.D: They cause rapid postoperative wound dehiscence

explanation: Old scar tissue can pull organs close to the abdominal wall, making them easier to accidentally nick when entering. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is a key reason for having the patient empty their bladder before laparoscopy?

options.A: To prevent accidental bladder injury during trocar insertion
options.B: To measure accurate baseline kidney function levels
options.C: To eliminate the need for general anesthesia agents
options.D: To prevent postoperative wound infection completely

explanation: A distended bladder sits higher in the pelvic cavity, making it vulnerable to puncture when inserting the initial instruments. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h4)

question: A patient complains of shoulder pain the day after laparoscopy. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Intravenous lines caused localized inflammation in the arm
options.B: The surgical incision site is radiating pain upward
options.C: The operating table position strained the shoulder muscles
options.D: Residual gas irritates the diaphragm and refers pain to the shoulder

explanation: Leftover gas presses against the nerve under the diaphragm, which the brain feels as pain up in the shoulder. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why is the patient often tilted head-down (Trendelenburg position) during pelvic laparoscopy?

options.A: Improve baseline respiratory exchange during anesthesia
options.B: Prevent deep vein thrombosis in the lower extremities
options.C: Shift abdominal organs away from the pelvic surgical field
options.D: Reduce the pressure of carbon dioxide insufflation

explanation: Gravity helps pull the intestines out of the pelvis so the surgeon can see the pelvic organs clearly. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h5)

question: Which nursing action is essential when positioning a patient for laparoscopic procedures?

options.A: Avoiding the use of safety straps to allow quick repositioning
options.B: Keeping the operating table completely flat at all times
options.C: Padding pressure points to prevent nerve injury during table tilting
options.D: Applying warm compresses to the lower extremities continuously

explanation: Extreme tilts can cause the patient to slide, putting pressure on nerves if proper padding and restraints are missing. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is a top priority for a nurse caring for a patient right after laparoscopy?

options.A: Signs of internal hemorrhage and vital sign changes
options.B: Immediate return of normal appetite and bowel habits
options.C: Complete wound healing at the trocar insertion sites
options.D: Normal physical strength in the lower extremities

explanation: Watching pulse and blood pressure helps catch any hidden bleeding inside the belly early. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why do nurses encourage patients to walk around early after surgery?

options.A: It speeds up the complete absorption of general anesthetic agents
options.B: It closes the small surgical incisions much faster
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for prescribed pain killers
options.D: It helps expel trapped gas and prevents blood clots

explanation: Walking gets the bowels moving, helps release trapped gas, and keeps blood flowing well in the legs. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is a major, life-threatening danger during the initial insertion of laparoscopic ports?
explanation: Inserting instruments blindly can sometimes lead to accidentally nicking big blood vessels deep in the belly. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h7)

question: A patient has a fever and a very hard, painful belly three days after surgery. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Referred pain originating from the shoulder tip
options.B: Normal physiological response to carbon dioxide gas
options.C: Minor subcutaneous emphysema around the port site

explanation: Severe pain, a rigid belly, and fever days later can mean the bowel leaked contents into the abdominal cavity. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h7)

question: What should a nurse tell a patient before they go home after a laparoscopy?

options.A: Remain on complete bed rest for at least one week
options.B: Keep the surgical incisions covered with waterproof tape for a month
options.C: Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous physical activities
options.D: Restrict fluid intake to prevent abdominal swelling

explanation: Avoiding heavy lifting keeps pressure off the small cuts so they heal without forming hernias. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h8)

question: A patient who just went home calls the clinic to report a new fever and worse belly pain. What is the nurse's best advice?

options.A: Apply a hot water bottle to the abdomen to relieve cramps
options.B: Return to the hospital promptly for medical evaluation
options.C: Wait another week to see if the symptoms resolve on their own
options.D: Take extra pain medication and rest in bed for another day

explanation: Fever and worsening pain are warning signs that need a doctor to check for infection or injury right away. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h8)
